Initial reaction rates v (uM/min) of a purified enzyme were measured at substrate concentrations S (uM) (no inhibitor, I = 0). Each condition was measured in duplicate; rates carry additive measurement noise.

The data table has 20 rows with columns: S, v. Your model will be used to predict rates at substrate levels outside the measured range.

Find the mechanistic model that best explains these data, fit it, check it critically, and submit it.

content.thinking:
I'm checking the data for a sigmoidal shape at low S, and the S=0.6 pair disagrees a lot (about -0.009 against 0.614), so that point looks noisy. The rest rises steadily with S, with the two readings at each level fairly close until around S=2.

I'm testing whether a Hill function fits better than Michaelis-Menten here, since the low-S values sit well under what MM would predict. A Hill curve with a Vmax near 10 and n around 2 tracks most points closely, though it comes out a little high at S=1 and S=2, so I'm trying a slightly different K to tighten the fit.

I'm checking the candidate values, trying K=2.9 and n=2 with Vmax at 10. Those fit most points well, though the curve runs a bit low at mid-range S, so I'm weighing whether a slightly higher Vmax would balance it.

content.text: {"mechanism_label": "hill", "params": {"Vmax": 10.0, "K": 2.9, "n": 2.0}, "custom_code": null, "confidence": 0.7, "reasoning": "The rate plateaus near 10 µM/min, but the low-S rates (about 0.3 at S=0.5 and 0.8 at S=1) fall well below what Michaelis-Menten predicts for a half-maximal point near S≈3, so the curve is sigmoidal. A Hill model with n≈2 and K≈2.9 reproduces the half-saturation near S≈3 and the plateau, though the exact n and K were estimated by eye."}
